LockedThe cast

One man, one woman, and a hundred of her. He is the only bare face in the house and he never lip‑syncs — his beats to camera are held stares.

HERW2. Jet black hair, sharpest cheekbones. The gold filigree half‑mask, black silk, opera gloves, red lips — the only colour in the film.cast

The call you left to usThe court stands

The dance vocabulary you liked is all still there — it just happens upright, where the camera can see it:

on the floorstanding
bodies rise to kneeling, arms up, dropthe crowd drops into a deep plié and rises, arms lifting together
backs arching, rolling down a rowa ripple of torsos arching back, rolling down the line one body after the next
legs slicing up in sequencearms slicing straight up in sequence — same wave, at head height
heads snapping together on the snareunchanged — the mass head‑turn is the signature
a body lying, one leg raiseda body leaning out of the line, held at an impossible angle by the bodies beside it
The floor is kept — twice, and only twice. The first image of the film: the camera comes through the lit window wall and finds a hundred bodies laid out on the stone in a pattern, dead still; they stand as the first verse begins and do not go down again. Then at 2:19, on his single clap, the whole room drops to the floor as one for four bars, and rises for the finale. Used twice, it lands. Used for three minutes, it is wallpaper.

Rebuilt from your notesThe house

One house, one night, modern electric light, windows in every room. Each of these is the actual plate the film’s shots are generated from — so the space cannot drift between shots.

The houseA modern castle on the ridge: stone ramparts, a square tower, a walled forecourt, a private road, the city below. Opens the film at night, closes it at dawn.
The ballroomLimestone washed by hidden strip light, glass chandeliers, a window wall onto the city, dark polished stone. Where the court lives.
The mirror wallThe far end of the same room: bronze mirror facing the night glass, so the city repeats into the depth of the reflection. Her solo.
The corridor of dressesHer gowns on brass rails, the window wall down one side, the far end in blackness. He walks the line with her handprint on his shirt.
One palette, no exceptions. Black, bone white, warm stone and brass. The only colour anywhere in the film is red lips — hers, and her hundred. The city beyond the glass stays cold and distant.

What we need back

  1. The standing court — yes, or tell us to put them back down.
  2. The house and the rooms — yes, or one note each.
  3. Then we shoot. On your word the whole film goes into generation against these references.
